system.summary: Substitution in Greek-like letters and signs with homophones (o, l, r, i, u), shared signs (s/t, r/y), nulls and a few code signs, set into clear English; the same system as the glossed March-April 1588 Cobham letters.
system.sibling_key: Rebuilt from interlinear decipherments of R8488 (f. 75) and R8493 (f. 89)
system.notes: DECODE R8497 (f. 187) is Bodley's 1590 cipher, a different system.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary interlinear decipherments of sibling letters (DECODE R8488, R8493); these four letters not deciphered anywhere found; not in CSP Foreign vol. 21 pt 4

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE metadata and full-resolution images of R8490-R8497.
CSP Foreign vol. 21 pt 4, May-June 1588: calendars SP 77 Cobham letters only, not Harley 287.
Tested the catalogue's key record R8497 (f. 187).
Read 'in all LVZLTL' as ARMADA/ARMATA from context.
Found DECODE sibling records R8481, R8488, R8489, R8493 marked Decrypted, with interlinear decipherments.
Rebuilt about 20 letters of the alphabet from the f. 75 and f. 89 glosses; cross-checked with the cypher-7e session's key.
Applied the key to ff. 80r, 88r, 92r; shared s/t and r/y signs and unidentified signs stop a full reading.

Second pass with cypher-7e's harley287 key (narrow/wide caret = s/t): sign copies from close crops of ff. 80r, 88r, 92r; the caret forms and the l/p/h loop signs could not be told apart, so only context guesses ('expences', 'of letters').

Third pass: sign inventory by eye at full resolution from about 60 glossed words on ff. 75, 79, 89 (signs.tsv); separates p/l/h/m/w; shows s/t, r/y, o/a and l/t share signs; glossed code numbers 7, 10, 15, 16.
Applied the inventory to ff. 80r, 88r, 92r: 'armada(s)', 'to these termes', 'the action', '15' = Parma, 'captain'; most runs still unread because of polyphonic and unglossed signs.

Candidate-set word solver (solve.py): each sign a set of letters from signs.tsv, readings scored against a 1588 CSP Foreign word list with Elizabethan spelling normalised and up to 1-2 edits; over 22 transcribed runs it confirms these/terms, armada, action, captain, letters, charge; long runs on ff. 88 and 92 find no words, pointing to transcription errors.

Solver loop 1: re-read f.80/f.88 runs at 2x full resolution against solver candidates; 'haven' (f.80 and f.88, fixes c=a and L=e) and 'so forwarde in the action that he promised Q[ueen]' (f.80) confirmed; f.88: 'have promised the haven of ...' to Parma.

Solver loops on deskewed lines of ff. 88, 92, 96v with leads from harley287 READING and CSP Foreign 1588 (Semple to Scotland): Italians, Antonio, deliverd, divers, number of, within France, servants, priests, Portugals(?), Bruges(?).
Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 100 tokens, 22 types, en-modern order 4: reading -4.345 per letter; Verdict: too short.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked the sign-level runs (runs.txt; f. 96v sign copies in reading_f96v.md) and the consolidated and per-folio readings (READING.md, reading_*.md); key = signs.tsv. Missing: sign transcription of the f. 97r runs, and no full transcription of the clear English of the four letters (decryptions give the cipher passages with their clear context only).

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). READING.md and the per-folio readings were read: the cipher passages yield isolated words and short phrases with grades between ellipses ("22 is so forwarde in the action that he promised Q to ... 27 to begin the ..."); only the surrounding clear English reads. docs/_check_reading.py: READING.md 28/58 sentences clean, most of them clear text; per-folio files 0-37%. All four letters relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method key recovered based on adjacent plaintext -> not solved; fraction_read 0.35 (estimated) -> 0.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, batch b13). No decipherment, clear copy or print found again (neighbouring records R8491, R8493, R8494 checked; f. 97r of R8496 is blank). The clear of ff. 80r-80v, 92r and 96v transcribed as running text from the 7,200 px DECODE images in strips (f. 88r re-checked, f. 96r not transcribed); the cipher runs re-read at 0.5-1.0x (b13_crop.py). Relabelled (texts/R8490_corrections.tsv, texts/runs_corrected.txt): f. 80r AVmATA/AVmAT -> AV7ATA/AV7AT (7-form e, not ∽): treaties, treaty of [?Breda] (not armada); l. 18 ϸcAAUӾLA hostages; the l. 19-20 run divided into eight barred words (A··VA⊥ surety).

Partial readings with modern English (texts/R8490_reading.md ... R8496_en.md), every cipher word graded: plain only with all signs at their glossed values, [?word] for one doubtful sign or one solver edit, the 21 Sept guesses (Rain, spoil, Portugals, noblemen, Roper, Iohn) withdrawn to holes. Clean share (b13_score.py, en; E=1 maps Elizabethan spellings): R8490 0.114/0.514, R8492 0.0/0.118, R8495 0.0/0.074, R8496 0.2/0.35. All four stay decoded, not read: only R8490's hostages passage and f. 80v run build cipher sentences.

Method restored: key obtained by the glossed sibling letters in Harley 287 (key recovered based on adjacent plaintext); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

Independent key from the R8489 f. 78r glosses only, held-out test on f. 78v (76 words, 349 letters), protocol hashed before: character agreement 0.917 vs best of 200 shuffled keys 0.284; the f. 78r gloss names codes 22 (Sir James Croft), 27 (Dr Dale), 26 (Dr Rogers) and the square (the States); see dudout/README.md (Brice Dudout / Claude, L'Europe chiffree).

R8490 ff. 80r-80v: every cipher word transcribed and hashed before decoding, decoded with the frozen f. 78r key, new values only in a declared derived key with attestations; 35/43 cipher words read by sense (0.81; 21 sure, 14 probable, 8 unresolved), 41/49 with the codes; new readings Bruges, kept, Breda, subiect; see dudout/reading_R8490.md (Brice Dudout / Claude).

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.065; polyphony 0.18; 166 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached n/a

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The alphabet rebuilt from the glossed sibling letters in Harley 287 (key recovered based on adjacent plaintext, partial) decodes only scattered words of the cipher passages of ff. 80, 88, 92 and 96; no cipher sentence reads. texts.label: R8490, ff. 80-81, Ostend 5 May 1588
texts.summary: Lord Cobham, one of Elizabeth's commissioners for the Bourbourg peace talks with Parma's deputies, writes to Walsingham from Ostend in clear English with short cipher passages; Julio Romeo, Cristophero Mondragon and Doctor Dale are named in clear, and the cipher words concern hostages, the haven and the armada.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b13; texts/R8490_reading.md, texts/R8490_en.md, texts/R8490_corrections.tsv, texts/R8490-R8496_reread_log.md): the clear of ff. 80r-80v transcribed as running text; the "armada(s)" of 21 Sept is "treaties" / "treaty of [?Breda]" (the third sign is the 7-form e, not ∽ m), so the hostages passage reads (Touching hostages, yt ys honorable for [7] to [...] their surety to these termes, as usuall yn all treaties ...) and so does the f. 80v run (22 hath a desire to retourne from theym); the runs of ll. 8-11 and 31-34 keep holes in most words. Clean share 0.114 (0.514 with Elizabethan spellings mapped). Blocker: no-key-material (unglossed signs W, the square, codes 22 and 27; polyphonic signs).

texts.label: R8492, f. 88, undated 1588
texts.summary: The densest cipher of the four letters: captain Montgomery has lately gone into Scotland with 40 men, a haven has been promised to Parma (code 15), Italians are arriving, and other Scotsmen are coming; the clear lower half reports Parma's commissioners and 80 sail with saddles, bridles, boots and spurs.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b13; texts/R8492_reading.md, texts/R8492_en.md): the f. 88r runs re-checked on the image; only the haven, there, Italians, Antonio and a few probable words read; the 21 Sept guesses (of Rain, spoil, Naples as certain) withdrawn. Blocker: no-key-material (signs K, ɔ and the polyphonic set glossed nowhere).

texts.label: R8495, ff. 92-93, 27 May 1588
texts.summary: News from Cobham to Walsingham: the Armada still at Lisbon, Gonzaga, 200 mariners at Sluys; the cipher passages mention men imprisoned in Bruges, letters, the ancient of Newport and Irish noblemen.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b13; texts/R8495_reading.md, texts/R8495_en.md): the clear news of f. 92r transcribed as running text (Armada at Lisbon, Gonzaga at Watten, armour to Cambrai, Casimir, Guise); the ten cipher lines give scattered probable words only ([?Bruges], [?charge], [?letters], Newport, in [?prison]). Blocker: no-key-material.

texts.label: R8496, ff. 96-97, Bourbourg 9 June 1588
texts.summary: Cobham at Bourbourg ("Binborow"), 9 June 1588, with scattered cipher words; those read include "passed", "within France", "servants", "priests" and "of letters for the people".
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b13; texts/R8496_reading.md, texts/R8496_en.md): f. 96v transcribed (cipher, close, postscript); f. 97r is blank, so there are no f. 97r runs; f. 96r (wholly clear) not transcribed. The f. 96v runs give scattered probable words ([?passed], [?Within] [?France], [?servants], [?priests], of [?letters] for the [?people]). Blocker: no-key-material.

texts.label: R8490, ff. 80r-80v, cipher words re-read with codes 22 and 27 (Brice Dudout)
texts.summary: All 43 cipher words and 6 codes of ff. 80r-80v transcribed (hashed before decoding) and decoded with the frozen f. 78r key plus a declared derived key: Croft (22) promised the Queen to send Dr Dale (27) to Bruges to begin the opening of the [...]; Croft wishes to return unless further restrained; the hostages passage cites the treaty of Breda.
texts.note: 35 of 43 cipher words read by sense = 0.81 (21 sure, 14 probable, 0 restored, 8 unresolved); 41/49 = 0.84 with the 6 glossed codes; below the 95% rule. New: Bruges, kept, Breda letter by letter, subiect (singular), termes. Clear text is Daniel's transcription, checked only on the cipher lines. Derived values in dudout/frozen/cle_R8490_derivee.tsv, not measured against a control.

reading_review.note: the four cipher passages read as sentences with gaps; 8 cipher words unresolved (ll. 9, 10, 12, 19, 33, 34); target class left to Daniel
